arxiv-1810-07010.title: Realism about the Wave Function
arxiv-1810-07010.creator: Eddy Keming Chen
arxiv-1810-07010.description: Abstract A century after the discovery of quantum mechanics, the meaning of quantum mechanics still remains elusive. This is largely due to the puzzling nature of the wave function, the central object in quantum mechanics. If we are realists about quantum mechanics, how should we understand the wave function? What does it represent? What is its physical meaning?

arxiv-2105-01393.title: Energy-gap driven low-temperature magnetic and transport properties in Cr M 1 / 3 {}_{1/3}M S 2 ( M M = Nb or Ta)
arxiv-2105-01393.creator: T. J. Hicken, Z. Hawkhead, M. N. Wilson, B. M. Huddart, A. E. Hall, G. Balakrishnan, C. Wang, F. L. Pratt, S. J. Clark, T. Lancaster
arxiv-2105-01393.description: Abstract The helimagnets Cr M 1 / 3 {}_{1/3}M S 2 ( M M = Nb or Ta) have attracted renewed attention due to the discovery of a chiral soliton lattice (CSL) stabilized in an applied magnetic field, but reports of unusual low-temperature transport and magnetic properties in this system lack a unifying explanation.

arxiv-2105-08888.title: Flat Band Induced Negative Magnetoresistance in Multi-Orbital Kagome Metal
arxiv-2105-08888.creator: Jie Zhang, T. Yilmaz, J. W. R. Meier, J. Y. Pai, J. Lapano, H. X. Li, K. Kaznatcheev, E. Vescovo, A. Huon, M. Brahlek, T. Z. Ward, B. Lawrie, R. G. Moore, H. N. Lee, Y. L. Wang, H. Miao, B. Sales
arxiv-2105-08888.description: Abstract Electronic flat band systems are a fertile platform to host correlation-induced quantum phenomena such as unconventional superconductivity, magnetism and topological orders. While flat band has been established in geometrically frustrated structures, such as the kagome lattice, flat band-induced correlation effects especially in those multi-orbital bulk systems are rarely seen.

arxiv-2110-02596.title: Supplementary Material
arxiv-2110-02596.description: Abstract I Histograms In Fig. 1 , histograms and KDEs are shown for the HOMO energies at the ZINDO, PBE0 and GW levels of QM7b molecules and for those at the B3LYP levels of QM9. The HOMO energies all follow unimodal distributions. Fig. 2 shows the same distributions for the LUMO energies.

arxiv-2203-14185.title: Identifying a minimal flavor symmetry of the seesaw mechanism behind neutrino oscillations
arxiv-2203-14185.description: Abstract In the canonical seesaw framework flavor mixing and CP violation in weak charged-current interactions of light and heavy Majorana neutrinos are correlated with each other and described respectively by the 3 × 3 3\times 3 matrices U U and R R .

arxiv-2305-07818.title: An Active Learning-based Approach for Hosting Capacity Analysis in Distribution Systems Thanks: Kiyeob Lee and Le Xie are with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Texas A&M University, College Station, TX, USA. Thanks: Peng Zhao, Anirban Bhattacharya and Bani K. Mallick are with t
arxiv-2305-07818.creator: Kiyeob Lee, Peng Zhao, Anirban Bhattacharya, Bani K. Mallick and Le Xie
arxiv-2305-07818.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kiyeob Lee, Peng Zhao, Anirban Bhattacharya, Bani K. Mallick and Le Xie. With the increasing amount of distributed energy resources (DERs) integration, there is a significant need to model and analyze hosting capacity (HC) for future electric distribution grids. Hosting capacity analysis (HCA) examines the amount of DERs that can be safely integrated into the grid and is a challenging task in full generality because there are many possible integration of DERs in foresight.

arxiv-2309-15817.title: Identifying the Risks of LM Agents with an LM-Emulated Sandbox
arxiv-2309-15817.creator: Yangjun Ruan, Honghua Dong, Andrew Wang, Silviu Pitis, Yongchao Zhou, Jimmy Ba, Yann Dubois, Chris J. Maddison, Tatsunori Hashimoto, University of Toronto Vector Institute Stanford University
arxiv-2309-15817.description: Abstract Recent advances in Language Model (LM) agents and tool use, exemplified by applications like ChatGPT Plugins, enable a rich set of capabilities but also amplify potential risks---such as leaking private data or causing financial losses. Identifying these risks is labor-intensive, necessitating implementing the tools, setting up the environment for each test scenario manually, and finding risky cases.

arxiv-2310-01731.title: The impact of social noise on the majority rule model across various network topologies
arxiv-2310-01731.creator: Roni Muslim, Didi Ahmad Mulya, Zulkaida Akbar, Rinto Anugraha NQZ
arxiv-2310-01731.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Roni Muslim, Didi Ahmad Mulya, Zulkaida Akbar, Rinto Anugraha NQZ. We explore the impact of social noise, characterized by nonconformist behavior, on the phase transition within the framework of the majority rule model. The order-disorder transition can reflect the consensus-polarization state in a social context. This study covers various network topologies, including complete graphs, two-dimensional (2-D) square lattices, three-dimensional (3-D) square lattices, and heterogeneous or complex networks such as Watts-Strogatz (W-S), Barabási-Albert (B-A), and Erdős-Rényi (E-R) networks, as well as their combinations (multilayer network).

arxiv-2506-14626.title: Spinning the Probe in Kerr with WQFT
arxiv-2506-14626.creator: Jitze Hoogeveen,
arxiv-2506-14626.description: Abstract HU-EP-25/22-RTG 1 Introduction The gravitational two-body problem — the classical dynamics of two massive point particles interacting through their gravitational attraction — is fundamental, conceptually simple and yet surprisingly complex. While the Newtonian case is integrable, the fully relativistic Einsteinian problem presents significant challenges.

arxiv-2507-03681.title: Robust estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects in randomized trials leveraging external data
arxiv-2507-03681.creator: Rickard Karlsson, Piersilvio De Bartolomeis, Issa J. Dahabreh, Jesse H. Krijthe
arxiv-2507-03681.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rickard Karlsson, Piersilvio De Bartolomeis, Issa J. Dahabreh, Jesse H. Krijthe. Randomized trials are typically designed to detect average treatment effects but often lack the statistical power to uncover effect heterogeneity over patient characteristics, limiting their value for personalized decision-making. To address this, we propose the QR-learner, a model-agnostic learner that estimates conditional average treatment effects (CATE) within the trial population by leveraging external data from other trials or observational studies.

arxiv-2508-15278.title: HostSub_GP : Precise Galaxy Background Subtraction in Transient Spectroscopy with Gaussian Processes Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , JAX ( Bradbury et al. 2018 ) , JAXopt ( Blondel et al. 2021 ) , tinygp ( Foreman-Mackey et al. 2024 ) , PypeIt ( Pr
arxiv-2508-15278.creator: Chang Liu (刘畅), Adam A. Miller
arxiv-2508-15278.description: Abstract We present a novel host galaxy subtraction technique in longslit spectroscopy for extragalactic transients. Unlike classic methods which generally estimate the background using a simple linear interpolation of local galaxy flux in the 2D spectrum, our approach leverages multi-band archival images of the host galaxies to model the background emission from the galaxy in the 2D spectrum.

arxiv-2508-20627.title: Monte Carlo simulation method for incoherent Thomson scattering spectra from arbitrary electron distribution functions
arxiv-2508-20627.creator: Ryo Yasuhara
arxiv-2508-20627.description: Abstract We developed a Monte Carlo simulation method to calculate incoherent Thomson scattering spectra in high temperature plasmas. The basic idea is to treat the entire scattering process as the superposition of individual photon-electron interactions. We introduce macro-particles, referred from particle-in-cell simulations, to reduce the computational cost, and obtain scattered spectra within a reasonable computational time.

arxiv-2511-23273.title: MUSIC: A Multi-Purpose Detector Concept for Physics at the 10 TeV Muon Collider
arxiv-2511-23273.creator: Paolo Andreetto, Nazar Bartosik, Andrea Bersani, Daniele Calzolari, Massimo Casarsa, Vittoria Ludovica Ciccarella, Elisa Di Meco, Ruben Gargiulo, Alessio Gianelle, Carlo Giraldin, Karol Krizka, Anton Lechner, Luigi Longo, Donatella Lucchesi, Leonardo Palombini, Nadia Pastrone, Ivano Sarra, Lorenzo S
arxiv-2511-23273.description: Abstract This work presents a proof of concept for MUSIC, a multi-purpose detector conceived for high-precision and ultra–high-energy physics studies in the challenging environment of s = 10 \sqrt{s}=10 TeV muon–antimuon collisions. The detector features a central tracking system, electromagnetic and hadronic calorimeters, and dedicated muon detectors.

arxiv-2512-06851.title: Controllable Emergence of Multiple Topological Anderson Insulator Phases in Photonic Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Lattices Preprint: This line only printed with preprint option
arxiv-2512-06851.creator: Ruijiang Ji, Yunbo Zhang, Shu Chen, Zhihao Xu
arxiv-2512-06851.description: Abstract We investigate the emergence and control of multiple topological Anderson insulator (TAI) phases in a one-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) waveguide lattice with generalized Bernoulli-type disorder introduced in the intradimer couplings. By systematically varying the disorder configuration—including the values and probabilities of the multivariate distribution—we demonstrate that both the number and width of TAI phases can be precisely engineered.

arxiv-2601-19382.title: Appraising the Necklace: A post-common-envelope carbon dwarf inside an apparently carbon-poor planetary nebula
arxiv-2601-19382.creator: David Jones, Romano L. M. Corradi, Gustavo A. García Pérez, Christophe Morisset, Jorge García-Rojas, Laurence Sabin, Bruce Balick, Jacob Wise, Antonio Mampaso, James Munday, Pablo Rodríguez-Gil, María del Mar Rubio-Díez, Miguel Santander-García, Paulina Sowicka, Alexander Csukai, Todd C. Hillwig, An
arxiv-2601-19382.description: Abstract Context. The Necklace nebula is a bipolar, post-common-envelope planetary nebula, the central star of which has been shown to have a dwarf carbon star companion. Aims. We aim to understand the origins of the Necklace and its dwarf carbon central star. Methods.

pmc-11352490.title: Resistance to Anti-HER2 Therapies in Gastrointestinal Malignancies
pmc-11352490.creator: Christiana Mo, Michelle Sterpi, Hyein Jeon, Fernand Bteich, Alain P Gobert
pmc-11352490.description: Simple SummaryFor many years, trastuzumab has remained a cornerstone in the treatment of HER2-positive cancers. However, primary and acquired resistance to trastuzumab and other HER2-targeted agents commonly prevents durable treatment responses in patients. The recent breakthroughs in HER2-targeted therapies for gastrointestinal malignancies necessitate a deeper understanding of resistance mechanisms and ways to circumvent them.

pmc-11452011.title: SMITE: Single Molecule Imaging Toolbox Extraordinaire (MATLAB)
pmc-11452011.creator: David J. Schodt, Michael J. Wester, Mohamadreza Fazel, Sajjad Khan, Hanieh Mazloom-Farsibaf, Sandeep Pallikkuth, Marjolein B. M. Meddens, Farzin Farzam, Eric A. Burns, William K. Kanagy, Derek A. Rinaldi, Elton Jhamba, Sheng Liu, Peter K. Relich, Mark J. Olah, Stanly L. Steinberg, Keith A. Lidke
pmc-11452011.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). SummaryFluorescence single molecule imaging comprises a variety of techniques that involve detecting individual fluorescent molecules. Many of these techniques involve localizing individual fluorescent molecules with precisions below the diffraction limit, which limits the spatial resolution of (visible) light-based microscopes.

pmc-12461296.title: Rapid and Reliable Determination of Free and Total Glycerol in Biodiesel by Iodometric Titration
pmc-12461296.creator: Gabriel M. Viegas, Leonardo M. Barbosa, Érica Barbosa de Sousa, Cristiane Gimenes, José G. Rocha Junior
pmc-12461296.description: Biodiesel is a renewable fuel produced by the transesterification of vegetable oils or animal fats. Regulatory agencies set strict limits on free and total glycerol levels in biodiesel intended for commercialization, as glycerol can impair combustion efficiency, promote engine deposits, and generate acroleina highly toxic aldehydeduring combustion.

pmc-12582454.title: Diagnosis of colorectal cancer using residual transformer with mixed attention and explainable AI
pmc-12582454.creator: Poonam Sharma, Bhisham Sharma, Ajit Noonia, Dhirendra Prasad Yadav, Panos Liatsis, Siamak Pedrammehr, Siamak Pedrammehr, Siamak Pedrammehr, Siamak Pedrammehr
pmc-12582454.description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the leading cause of cancer disease and poses a significant threat to global health. Although deep learning models have been utilized to accurately diagnose CRC, they still face challenges in capturing the global correlations of spatial features, especially in complex textures and morphologically similar features.

pmc-12599155.title: Grounded in culture: a participatory empowerment evaluation of the oskâyak (youth) power program for oskinîkiwak (young men) and napêsisak (boys) at pakitahaw sākahikan iýiniwak (sturgeon lake first nation)
pmc-12599155.creator: Norma Rabbitskin, Clifford Ballantyne, Udoka Okpalauwaekwe, Scott Tunison, Vivian R Ramsden
pmc-12599155.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The Oskâyak (Youth) Power Program (YPP) at Pakitahaw Sākahikan Iýiniwak (Sturgeon Lake First Nation) was co-created by and with youth to strengthen miyo-ayāwin (wellness) among oskinîkiwak (young men) and napêsisak (boys). Using a participatory empowerment evaluation grounded in a braided framework of community-based participatory research (CBPR), transformative learning, and ethical space, guided conversations were held with 14 youth supported by Kēhtēyak (Elders) and Kayāsi Kistēyihtamow Kanawēyihcikēw (Traditional Knowledge Keepers).

pmc-12715508.title: codonGPT: reinforcement learning on a generative language model enables scalable mRNA design
pmc-12715508.creator: Binita Rajbanshi, Anuj Guruacharya
pmc-12715508.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a powerful tool for design tasks in engineering. However, in biology, the combination of RL with language models has not been explored. Moreover, emerging generative language models for biology focus on DNA, non-coding RNA, or proteins. This ignores information hidden in coding messenger RNA (mRNA).

pmc-12817415.title: Relevance and consequence of economic and social resources of severely ill persons and their informal caregivers at the end-of-life: a systematic review of qualitative studies
pmc-12817415.creator: Marlene Matzinger, Eleonore Baum, Daniela Bernhardsgrütter, Miriam Kesseli, Gerald Michelak, Fabiola Orosaj, Andrea Kobleder, Janine Vetsch
pmc-12817415.description: BackgroundLife-limiting illnesses often lead to complex care needs and multifaceted support requirements for both severely ill persons and their informal caregivers, particularly at the end of life. The extent to which these needs are met may be significantly influenced by available economic and social resources. However, an in-depth understanding of how such resources shape end-of-life experiences is still missing.

pmc-13115983.title: Understanding Glioblastoma Dynamics Using 3D Organoids and Engineered Extracellular Matrix
pmc-13115983.creator: Autumn McManis, Charles Ashley Jimenez, Abha Shirolkar, Syed Raza ur Rehman, Sumana Mallick, Malea Murphy, Akhilesh K. Gaharwar, Irtisha Singh
pmc-13115983.description: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is an aggressive, angiogenic WHO grade IV glioma marked by rapid progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis. A defining feature of GBM is the presence of glioma stem‐like cells (GSC), which reside in specialized perivascular niches and drive tumor progression, recurrence, and therapeutic resistance.

pmc-13224274.title: The role of dordaviprone in the multidisciplinary management of diffuse midline glioma
pmc-13224274.creator: Abdullah M. Al Lawati, Mohammed K. Al Suleimani, Iman A. Al Rasbi, Mohammed A. Al Hinai, Sara B. Al Marbouai, Hoor B. Al Barhi, Hanan M. Al Lawati, Ghusn S. Al Sideiri
pmc-13224274.description: Background: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is a rare and aggressive pediatric and young adult brain tumor arising from midline structures of the central nervous system. Surgical resection is not possible due to its infiltrative nature, and radiotherapy remains the only standard treatment with limited benefit. Chemotherapy has failed to improve survival because of poor blood–brain barrier (BBB) penetration.

pmc-13245341.title: Mitral Valve Lymphoma: An Unusual Cause of Embolic Strokes
pmc-13245341.creator: Atharv Oak, Abdullah Arain, Uzma Rahman, Sumera I. Yilmaz, Jesse Suben, Ahmet Kilic
pmc-13245341.description: An 80-year-old woman with a history of non-Hodgkin lymphoma and branch retinal artery occlusion presented with acute visual changes and received a diagnosis of multifocal embolic cerebral infarcts. Cardiac imaging revealed a mobile left atrial mass on the mitral valve. Surgical excision was undertaken because of the high risk of recurrent embolization and strokes.

pmc-13583908.title: Design and Synthesis of Novel 1,2,3‐Triazole Conjugates Featuring Hydroxamic Acid and Sulfonamide Moieties: Exploring Dual Pharmacophores for Enhanced Biological Activity
pmc-13583908.creator: Dineshkumar Pagar, Ranjay Shaw, Hemant Suryavanshi, Dhanji Rajani, Sudhakar Patil
pmc-13583908.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A new series of N‐hydroxy‐1‐(4‐(aryl sulfonamido)phenyl)‐1H‐1,2,3‐triazole‐4‐carboxamide derivatives (8a‐j) were synthesized through a concise multistep route integrating three key pharmacophores: the 1,2,3‐triazole core, an aryl sulfonamide moiety, and an N‐hydroxycarboxamide group. Biological evaluation demonstrated promising antimicrobial potential for several derivatives. Compounds 8f, 8g, and 8i exhibited notable antibacterial activity against both Gram‐positive and Gram‐negative bacteria, whereas most analogues showed weak antifungal activity.

pmc-13677959.title: Indications, procedural standards, and training requirements for flexible nasolaryngoscopy in pulmonology – a Delphi study protocol✰
pmc-13677959.creator: Ajit Nair, Philip G Bardin, Paul Leong
pmc-13677959.description: Flexible nasolaryngoscopy (FNL) is a well-established, minimally invasive procedure for assessing the nasal passages, nasopharynx, and larynx. Its role in pulmonology is expanding, particularly for evaluating vocal cord dysfunction/inducible laryngeal obstruction, chronic cough, and other upper airway conditions relevant to the “united airways” model of care.
